alpha.meaning: Return the model expects beyond what the market and known factors explain
alpha.formula: alpha = E[r] minus beta times market return
alpha.typical: A few tenths of a percent a month is already large

volatility.meaning: Standard deviation of returns, scaled to a year
volatility.typical: Large US stocks 15 to 40 percent a year

prob_positive.meaning: Posterior probability that the signal's true mean return is above zero after shrinkage
prob_positive.typical: Above 0.9 is strong. Near 0.5 means no information

sharpe.meaning: Mean excess return divided by its standard deviation, annualized
sharpe.formula: SR = mean / sd times sqrt(12) for monthly data
sharpe.typical: 0.5 is decent for one signal. Above 2 usually means an error or overfitting

trial_count.meaning: Every variant tested, kept or not. More trials make a lucky result more likely
trial_count.typical: Compare a Sharpe ratio with this number before trusting it

slippage_bps.meaning: Fill price compared with the quote midpoint at arrival, in basis points
slippage_bps.formula: side times (fill minus mid) / mid times 10000

signal_strength.meaning: Model output before calibration. It is not a probability or a forecast return
signal_strength.typical: Only the sign and rank are used until calibration exists

tier.meaning: Evidence tier from 1 (idea) to 6. Academic evidence stops at 3. Tier 4 needs a test on real data. Tier 5 needs prospective results and Aditi
tier.typical: Only tiers 4 and up can carry capital

economic.meaning: Result of the walk-forward research portfolio at double the modeled costs

basis.meaning: Empirical comes from a cited result. Safeguard limits damage and only Aditi changes it. Provisional is a starting setting under review. External fact has a source and a date

adv20.meaning: Average dollar volume over the last 20 sessions
adv20.typical: Orders here stay under a small share of it

daily_return.plain: How much it moved in a day
daily_return.meaning: Change in closing price from one session to the next, as a fraction of the earlier close
daily_return.typical: Large US stocks usually move under 2 percent a day

standard_error.meaning: Standard deviation of an estimate across samples. A mean with a large standard error could easily be zero
standard_error.formula: se = sd / sqrt(n) for independent observations
standard_error.typical: Compare it with the estimate itself. A ratio above 1 means little information
